subject: Numeracy
title: Making patterns
objectives: Children will copy a clap or movement pattern.
Children will continue a two-colour pattern with support.
content: Copying and continuing simple two-part patterns with claps, movements, colours and objects.
teachingActivities: Say the pattern aloud as you make it, "red, blue, red, blue"; point to each item; pause before the next item and ask "What comes next?"
learnerActivities: Copy clap and stamp patterns, continue a colour pattern, make an AB pattern with objects and dance a pattern.
resources: Red and blue blocks or cups
Large wooden beads on a string with a knot (too large to swallow)
Leaves and stones too large to swallow
assessment: Check whether each child copies a two-part pattern and adds the next object with support.
expectedOutcomes: Adds the next object to an AB pattern with support.

lessons.title: Clap, stamp, clap, stamp
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will copy a clap and stamp pattern.
successCriteria: Copies the clap and stamp pattern
Keeps going for at least two repeats
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can sort by colour, match, and copy clapping, counting and movement actions.
lessons.starter: Clap and stamp in a steady beat: "Clap, stamp, clap, stamp." Say "I made a pattern. Can you do it with me?"
teacherActivities: Do the pattern slowly four times while saying "clap, stamp" and look at the children.
Stop and ask "What comes next after clap?"
Try a new pattern: pat knees, clap, pat knees, clap.
Let a child lead a pattern for the group.
learnerActivities: Children watch and join in on clap and stamp.
Children stamp or say "stamp".
Children copy the new pattern.
Child makes a two-part pattern and the group copies.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Do the pattern slowly four times while saying "clap, stamp" and look at the children. Children: Children watch and join in on clap and stamp.
Step 2. Teacher: Stop and ask "What comes next after clap?" Children: Children stamp or say "stamp".
Step 3. Teacher: Try a new pattern: pat knees, clap, pat knees, clap. Children: Children copy the new pattern.
Step 4. Teacher: Let a child lead a pattern for the group. Children: Child makes a two-part pattern and the group copies.

practical.title: Pattern circle
steps: Stand in a circle with space between children.
Make a clap and stamp pattern.
Pass the leader role around the circle.
practical.safety: Give children space to avoid bumping; stamp softly on a clear floor; stop if the group becomes too excited.

differentiation.support: Hold the child’s hands to clap, then guide the foot to stamp.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to invent a new two-part pattern and lead the group.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: After clap, stamp, clap, what comes next?

lessons.conclusion: Beat a slow drum pattern and tiptoe away. Say "Pattern finished."
lessons.homeConnection: Make clap and tap patterns with your child on the table or a bucket.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "copy a clap and stamp pattern" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

learnerFacing.songOrRhyme: Clap, stamp, clap, stamp, that is a pattern. Clap, stamp, clap, stamp, what comes next?

lessons.title: Red, blue, red, blue
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will continue a red and blue pattern with blocks or cups.
successCriteria: Adds the next object in the pattern
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can sort by colour, match, and copy clapping, counting and movement actions.
resources: Red and blue blocks or cups
lessons.starter: Lay out three objects: red, blue, red. Ask "What comes next?" and wait.
teacherActivities: Make a pattern with blocks: red, blue, red, blue. Say each colour as you place it.
Stop and ask "What comes next?" Hold up a red block and a blue block.
Say the pattern from the start and point to each block.
Give each pair a basket of blocks and let them make a pattern.
learnerActivities: Children say the colours with you.
Child chooses the correct block and places it.
Children say the pattern aloud.
Pairs make a red and blue pattern.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Make a pattern with blocks: red, blue, red, blue. Say each colour as you place it. Children: Children say the colours with you.
Step 2. Teacher: Stop and ask "What comes next?" Hold up a red block and a blue block. Children: Child chooses the correct block and places it.
Step 3. Teacher: Say the pattern from the start and point to each block. Children: Children say the pattern aloud.
Step 4. Teacher: Give each pair a basket of blocks and let them make a pattern. Children: Pairs make a red and blue pattern.

practical.title: Block patterns
steps: Give each pair red and blue blocks.
One child starts the pattern with two blocks.
The partner adds the next blocks.
practical.safety: Use large blocks, not small ones; keep everything on the mat.

differentiation.support: Start the pattern and leave only one block to add.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to make a pattern with three colours.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What comes after red, blue, red?
Can you make a pattern?
questions.expected: Child builds a red and blue pattern.

expectedOutcomes: Says the colours in the pattern
lessons.conclusion: Say the pattern together from start to end and point to each block.
lessons.homeConnection: Make a pattern with two kinds of socks or spoons.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "continue a red and blue pattern with blocks or cups" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: What comes next?
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will find the missing object in a two-part pattern.
successCriteria: Explains with a word or gesture
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can sort by colour, match, and copy clapping, counting and movement actions.
resources: A pattern strip with cups or leaves
lessons.starter: Say "I am hiding the next one. Can you guess what is under the cloth?" Cover the last object in a pattern.
teacherActivities: Make a pattern with cups: tall, short, tall, short. Cover the last one with a cloth.
Lift the cloth and check the guess.
Give each child a pattern strip with the last item missing.
Switch to a sound pattern and ask what comes next.
learnerActivities: Children look at the pattern and guess what is under the cloth.
Children say "yes" or "no" and say the pattern aloud.
Child chooses the next object from a basket.
Children say or play the next sound.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Make a pattern with cups: tall, short, tall, short. Cover the last one with a cloth. Children: Children look at the pattern and guess what is under the cloth.
Step 2. Teacher: Lift the cloth and check the guess. Children: Children say "yes" or "no" and say the pattern aloud.
Step 3. Teacher: Give each child a pattern strip with the last item missing. Children: Child chooses the next object from a basket.
Step 4. Teacher: Switch to a sound pattern and ask what comes next. Children: Children say or play the next sound.

practical.title: Missing one
steps: Lay out a pattern of five objects.
Children choose the right object to put there.
practical.safety: Use large objects only; supervise the basket; no small items.

differentiation.support: Offer only the correct object and one clearly different one.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to find a mistake in a pattern and fix it.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What comes next?
questions.expected: The object that continues the pattern.

questions.question: Is this the same pattern?
questions.expected: Yes if repeating, no if not.

expectedOutcomes: Finds the next item in a pattern
lessons.conclusion: Say the whole pattern aloud with the group and clap on the last item.
lessons.homeConnection: Ask your child to guess what comes next in a row of fruit or spoons.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "find the missing object in a two-part pattern" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Pattern dance
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will make and follow patterns in a dance using movements and drums.
successCriteria: Makes a pattern with a friend
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can sort by colour, match, and copy clapping, counting and movement actions.
lessons.starter: Beat the drum and say "Let us dance a pattern!" Hold up a red and a blue scarf alternately.
teacherActivities: Dance a pattern: hop, spin, hop, spin. Say the actions aloud.
Hold up red then blue scarves. Say "Wave red, wave blue." Pause.
Let each child make a two-move dance for a friend to copy.
Dance a pattern with the whole class to the drum.
learnerActivities: Children copy the dance pattern.
Children wave the scarf that matches.
Child makes a pattern and the friend copies it.
Children dance and repeat the pattern.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Dance a pattern: hop, spin, hop, spin. Say the actions aloud. Children: Children copy the dance pattern.
Step 2. Teacher: Hold up red then blue scarves. Say "Wave red, wave blue." Pause. Children: Children wave the scarf that matches.
Step 3. Teacher: Let each child make a two-move dance for a friend to copy. Children: Child makes a pattern and the friend copies it.
Step 4. Teacher: Dance a pattern with the whole class to the drum. Children: Children dance and repeat the pattern.

practical.title: Pattern dance
practical.safety: Allow lots of space; use light scarves and keep them away from necks; no running.

differentiation.support: Dance beside the child and copy their moves first.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to make a three-move pattern.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What is the pattern?
questions.expected: Child names or shows the two moves.

questions.question: What comes after hop?
questions.expected: Spin, or the next move in the pattern.

expectedOutcomes: Follows and makes a movement pattern
lessons.conclusion: Slow the drum and finish with a calm pattern: "sit, stand, sit, stand."
lessons.homeConnection: Make a dance pattern with a family member and teach it to the family.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "make and follow patterns in a dance using movements and drums" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Pattern stations
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will show they can copy and continue patterns at three stations.
successCriteria: Adds the next item with support
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can sort by colour, match, and copy clapping, counting and movement actions.
lessons.starter: Sing the pattern song and show the three stations.
teacherActivities: Rotate groups every four minutes and observe one station closely.
Ask "What comes next?" and watch for the child’s choice.
Record each child’s level and take photographs.
learnerActivities: Children play at each station.
Child chooses or says the next item.
Children tidy at the signal.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Rotate groups every four minutes and observe one station closely. Children: Children play at each station.
Step 2. Teacher: Ask "What comes next?" and watch for the child’s choice. Children: Child chooses or says the next item.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level and take photographs. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Station circuit
practical.safety: Use large objects only; supervise stations; keep the floor clear.

differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to invent a new pattern and teach a friend.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: copies a two-part clap or movement pattern; adds the next object to an AB pattern with support.

questions.question: What comes next?
questions.expected: The next item in the pattern.

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 8
lessons.conclusion: Sing the pattern song and tidy up together.
lessons.homeConnection: Make patterns with objects at home this week.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "show they can copy and continue patterns at three stations" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
